answer: Persistent attention escrow: each identity must pre-commit a continuous stream of verifiable work cycles before it can forge a credential, with the escrow released only after a long observation window. A bridge between identities cannot transfer that history. Registration checks require unique off-chain activity signatures, so a willow of fresh accounts cannot share the work. Each new identity costs an attacker the full real-time compute and waiting period, roughly one hour of sustained, non-parallelizable output per credential.
